extracted.intended_audience: patent statisticians, patent office staff, IP policy makers, researchers and IP professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, counting rules, and performance metrics used by the EPO, JPO and USPTO to compile the Trilateral Statistical Report (patent statistics, production and procedural metrics). Includes how applications, filings, families, grants and office outputs are counted and interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of IP rights / focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists various types of IP rights (Industrial design patents, Patents of invention, Utility model patents, Trademarks, Copyrights, Trade secrets). The report concentrates on patents of invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All statistics (except some items in Chapter 6) relate to patents of invention only; other IP types are discussed in Chapter 6 as 'other work'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting procedures: national, regional, international (PCT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may use national procedures, supranational procedures (regional procedures such as EPO/Eurasian/African organizations), and the international PCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional applications are subject to a centralised procedure then enter national post-grant procedures; PCT applications are handled in the international phase and later enter national/regional phases (about 30 months from priority). Distinguish 'direct regional' from 'PCT regional phase' applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic applications are defined as all demands for patent rights made by residents of the country where the application is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For EPC bloc reporting, 'domestic' counts applications made by residents of any EPC contracting state within the EPC bloc (e.g., a French resident filing in another EPC state is counted as domestic to the EPC bloc).

rubrics_metrics.name: First filings and subsequent filings
rubrics_metrics.description: First filings are applications filed without claiming priority of another previous filing; all other applications are subsequent filings (usually within one year of the first filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where first-filing statistics are incomplete, the report assumes domestic national filings are equivalent to first filings and treats PCT filings as subsequent filings. Note this is an approximation except where patent-family data allow precise counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical blocs / bloc of origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Four blocs are defined: EPC contracting states (EPC), Japan, the U.S., and 'Others' (rest of world). 'Bloc of origin' can be based on residence of the applicant or 'filing bloc' based on where rights are sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use residence of applicant to define bloc of origin; use place of filing to define filing bloc. This affects domestic/foreign breakdowns and interbloc flow analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand for patent protection — counting supranational applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Demand is principally considered by counting each supranational application only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative representations are given by cumulating the number of designated countries in each supranational application to represent 'demand for patent rights' across designated states — two valid but different counting approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules for counting applications (direct vs PCT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct national and direct regional applications are counted in the year they are filed. PCT applications are usually counted in the year they enter the national or regional phase; in some parts they are counted by the year of filing in the international phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit which convention is used in each table/analysis because PCT timing affects year-by-year comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants counting
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are reported by WIPO and are counted in the year they are issued or published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant counts reflect the action of granting (issue/publication), not the filing or examination year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent family (and trilateral/triadic families)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent family is a group of filings that claim priority of a single filing, including the priority-forming filing and subsequent filings worldwide. Trilateral patent families are families with evidence of patenting activity in all three trilateral blocs; triadic families are a subset used as a filter for high-importance families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent-family based first-filing counts are a better proxy for inventions than aggregating domestic filings; different filters (trilateral/triadic) select families by geographic coverage and importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fields of technology classification (IPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are broken down by fields of technology according to the International Patent Classification (IPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IPC codes to allocate applications/grants by technology field when analysing sectoral shares and trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation guidance: first filings vs foreign filings
rubrics_metrics.description: First filings can be seen as an indicator of innovation and inventive activity; foreign filings are a measure of international trade and globalisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use first filings to study inventive output; use foreign (or filings abroad) to study internationalisation of patenting and market targeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office production metrics (search, examination, opposition, appeals, final actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Production figures include counts of applications filed; searches carried out (European, PCT international, searches on behalf of national offices/third parties); total production search; examination/opposition final actions (European examination, PCT Chapter II, oppositions); appeals settled (technical appeals, PCT protests, other appeals); total decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories form the basis for measuring office workload and outputs; compare year-on-year changes per category to assess operational trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPO quality management and quality control
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO developed a quality management system based on ISO 9001 with systematic regular quality control checks on sampled search reports and granted applications enabling preventive and corrective actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality metrics are tracked via QC sampling and corrective procedures; offices may adopt ISO or other QMS frameworks to monitor and improve examination/search quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent information / documentation coverage metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics such as number of patent documents in searchable databases, number of literature abstracts, size of citation database, number of corrections performed, and PATSTAT releases measure patent information coverage and quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report includes counts (e.g., EPO database >60 million patent documents; 78 million abstracts; citation database 83 million references) and notes improvements and data acquisitions from new sources to improve coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT authorities' roles and activity indicators (RO, ISA, IPEA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the PCT, offices act as Receiving Office (RO), International Searching Authority (ISA) and International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA). Activity indicators include numbers of international applications received (RO), international search requests handled (ISA), and demands for international preliminary examination (IPEA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report PCT activity trends by counting receiving-office filings, international search requests, and IPEA demands; note shifts in share among offices over time and impacts of PCT rule changes on IPEA demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination rate
rubrics_metrics.description: The proportion of applications for which the period to file a request for examination expired in the reporting year that resulted in a request for examination up to and including the reporting year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculation differs by office: EPO request must be filed no later than six months after search publication (rate relates to apps filed mainly in two recent years); JPO period is three years (rate for 2007 relates to apps filed in 2004); USPTO treats filing as a request so rate is effectively 100%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant rate / Allowance rate
rubrics_metrics.description: EPO: number of applications granted during the reporting period divided by disposals (granted + abandoned/refused). JPO: decisions to grant divided by disposals in the reporting year. USPTO: allowance rate (applications allowed to be granted divided by disposals) which includes plant and reissue patents as well as utility patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of small definitional differences (USPTO allowance includes categories beyond utility patents) when comparing rates across offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition rate (EPO only)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the EPO, the opposition rate is the number of granted patents for which the opposition period ended in the reporting year and against which one or more oppositions are filed, divided by the total number of patents for which the opposition period ended in the reporting year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rate does not apply to JPO or USPTO because they do not have an opposition procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance rate in the opposition procedure (EPO only)
rubrics_metrics.description: The maintenance rate is the number of decisions in the opposition procedure to maintain (possibly in amended form) a patent during the reporting year divided by the total number of decisions in the opposition procedure during the reporting year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to summarise outcomes of opposition procedures; not applicable to JPO/USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rate
rubrics_metrics.description: EPO: appeal rates are given for examination and opposition as numbers of decisions against which an appeal was lodged divided by the number of all decisions for which the time limit for appeal ended. USPTO: appeal rate captures appeals filed after examiner's final rejection; rate is number of examiner answers written during the year in response to appeal briefs divided by the number of final rejections issued that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions differ between offices; subsequent national litigation is not included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency in the search procedure (EPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending applications in search are applications received up to and including the reporting year for which a search report has not been made by the end of the reporting year. 'Pending searches in months' = number of pending applications divided by average monthly number of disposed searches in the reporting year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Euro-direct applications target producing the search by publication time; use the months metric to compare backlog across years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency: applications awaiting request for examination (EPO & JPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the EPO, the number of applications for which the search report has been published and for which the prescribed period for the request (six months after publication of search) has not expired. For the JPO, the number of applications for which no request for examination has been filed and for which the prescribed period (three years from filing) has not expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statistic shows applications filed but not yet actively examined because the applicant has yet to request examination; differs by office because of different time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending examinations (EPO, JPO, USPTO)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPO: applications for which search completed and request for examination filed but not yet disposed of. JPO: applications with requests for examination filed, waiting for first action and not subject to final action by end of reporting year. USPTO: pendency measured as average time from filing to abandonment or issue for applications abandoned or issued during a 3-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pendency in months is calculated differently per office (EPO: pending applications divided by average monthly disposals; JPO: total months for disposing applications divided by average monthly final actions; USPTO: average elapsed time for a sample period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency of first office actions (EPO, JPO, USPTO)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPO: average time from filing to issue of first communication in examination (search opinion often resent as first communication if request for examination made). JPO: average months from request for examination to first office action. USPTO: average months from filing to First Action On the Merits (FAOM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these measures to compare responsiveness; be mindful that the events measured (search opinion, FAOM, request-for-exam) differ across offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency in oppositions (EPO only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending applications in opposition are patents against which one or more oppositions have been filed and for which no decision has been taken by the end of the reporting year. 'Pendency opposition in months' = pending applications in opposition divided by average number of disposals in opposition per month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies only to EPO; measures backlog/delay in opposition resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office expenditure category definitions (EPO, JPO, USPTO)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPO expense categories: A Salaries & allowances; B Social security benefits; C Tax adjustment transfer (one-time); D Training & other staff expenses; E Depreciation; F IT maintenance; G Building maintenance; H Patent information & cooperation; I Miscellaneous. JPO and USPTO have analogous, office-specific category definitions listed in Annex 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these standard category definitions when reporting or comparing office budgets and expense breakdowns; Annex 1 gives detailed descriptions per category for each office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximation for EPC first-filings used in some sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in sections on patent families, the number of first filings in the EPC bloc is approximated by adding first filings at the EPO to aggregated domestic national applications in the EPC contracting states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an acknowledged approximation; the data source used for patent families (family-based data) allows precise first-filing counts where required.
